reuse.why: Routes all adjustments through the existing applyWeekendRule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend and recurConfigToRSchedule, and the new range handler reuses the same RSchedule/applyWeekendRule pipeline as getUpcomingDates.

duplication.why: getDatesInRange re-creates the getUpcomingDates schedule construction and adjust-map pipeline instead of sharing it, and the MM-DD holiday match is implemented twice (isYearlyHoliday/dayMatchesMonthDay for exdates vs str.slice(5) in isOff).

placement.why: Rule logic sits in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts as the tree does, though the daily 'skip' rule is split between rrule byDayOfWeek, a separate exdates builder and the shift helper.

scope.why: Changes stay on the schedule date rule, the new handler, types, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Every RSchedule construction must remember to pair recurConfigToRSchedule with recurConfigToExdates (find-schedules does not), exdates are expanded for 100 years, and the 14-day padding is an unexplained bound that holidays can exceed.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All date adjustments call applyWeekendRule; the daily skip is expressed through new shared helpers rather than around them.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts: yearly-holiday matching written once as isYearlyHoliday+dayMatchesMonthDay and again as holidaySet.has(str.slice(5)) inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend; schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange reshapes the getUpcomingDates pipeline.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays parameter added to applyWeekendRule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; daily byDayOfWeek branch in recurConfigToRSchedule and the MM-DD special case inside isOff; holiday skipping for daily schedules lives in a separate recurConfigToExdates that each RSchedule site must call.
